text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Saddam Hussein proposes a new saving system for government employees.
- Saddam says Iraq has become a bastion for Arabs.
- Iraq briefs Arab League on Turkish invasion of its north.
- U.N. sanctions committee passes more food contracts, and Iraq plans to hand out full food basket in July.
- Australia and Algeria sign oil deal.
- Chinese oil delegation arrives in Iraq.
- Iraq to open borders with Syria.
(The above were also carried by JUMHOURIA and AL-THAWRA)
- Article says Arabs cannot rely on America to defend them against enemies.
- Jordanian companies seek a boost in imports to Iraq.
- China to invest half a billion dollars in Ahdab oilfield.
- Experimental operation of Basra water project to start in the middle of this month.
- Commentary lambasts United States over Turkish invasion of northern Iraq.
- Anti-crime squads capture gang of thieves accused of 80 burglaries.
